summary: Scientists from the United Kingdom concluded in a genetic study of 6,000 ancient male skulls from around the world that modern humans originated in southeastern Africa—called "The Cradle of Man"—after comparing skull size and shape with later humans and DNA, with the oldest tested skull at least 40,000 years old, Andrea Manica of the Department of Zoology at the University of Cambridge said. Some scientists called the study "mistaken"; John Hawks of the University of Wisconsin-Madison said you cannot find the origin of people by measuring skull variability, criticized the paper for relying on genetic assumptions from 10 to 15 years ago that he says are now known to be wrong, and argued that Africa's ecological diversity and climate-related effects on skull size mean that correcting for climate subtracts a major component of variability.
